motion: The Middle East road map for peace is dead.

dropped_turns.text: I grant that the road map no longer drives daily decisions. But its framework can still return when conditions improve, so the motion is false.

Its language remains, but its leverage has gone.

turns.speaker: CON

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: This road map does not need active implementation. Its collapse already shows that a framework can linger on paper while losing authority, which is precisely why this particular road map is dead.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: Both statements fit because a living road map needs action, while this one has become evidence of what happens without it. Its paper survival is not political life; its absent implementation proves the motion.

turns.text: When both sides return to direct bargaining, the road map remains useful because it supplies familiar steps and a common vocabulary. That conditional value means it is dormant, not dead.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: A road map can survive long neglect if its goals remain necessary to any settlement. How can a document be dead while dialogue still circles the same destination it describes?

turns.text: Your "underlying framework" point confuses shared problems with a living plan. Any peace effort faces those problems, but this road map's own sequence has stopped commanding action, which makes it dead.
